legend: Every airport has a baggage claim area, and Balbesovo Airport is no exception. At some point, one of the administrators at Sheremetyevo came up with an unusual idea: to change the traditional shape of the baggage claim conveyor from a carousel to a more complex form.

Suppose that the baggage claim area is represented as a rectangular grid of size n×m%%ZSMJ0%%. The administration proposed that the path of the conveyor should pass through the cells p1,p2,…,p2k+1%%ZSMJ1%%, where pi=(xi,yi)%%ZSMJ2%%.

For each cell pi%%ZSMJ3%% and the next cell pi+1%%ZSMJ4%% (where 1≤i≤2k%%ZSMJ5%%), these cells must share a common side. Additionally, the path must be simple, meaning that for no pair of indices i≠j%%ZSMJ6%% should the cells pi%%ZSMJ7%% and pj%%ZSMJ8%% coincide.

Unfortunately, the route plan was accidentally spoiled by spilled coffee, and only the cells with odd indices of the path were preserved: p1,p3,p5,…,p2k+1%%ZSMJ9%%. Your task is to determine the number of ways to restore the original complete path p1,p2,…,p2k+1%%ZSMJ10%% given these k+1%%ZSMJ11%% cells.
Since the answer can be very large, output it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ12%%.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤t≤3⋅104%%ZSMJ14%%). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains three integers n%%ZSMJ15%%, m%%ZSMJ16%%, and k%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤n,m≤1000%%ZSMJ18%%, n⋅m≥3%%ZSMJ19%%, 1≤k≤⌊12(nm−1)⌋%%ZSMJ20%%) — the dimensions of the grid and a parameter defining the length of the path.

Next, there are k+1%%ZSMJ21%% lines, the i%%ZSMJ22%%-th of which contains two integers x2i−1%%ZSMJ23%% and y2i−1%%ZSMJ24%% (1≤x2i−1≤n%%ZSMJ25%%, 1≤y2i−1≤m%%ZSMJ26%%) — the coordinates of the cell p2i−1%%ZSMJ27%% that lies on the path.
It is guaranteed that all pairs (x2i−1,y2i−1)%%ZSMJ28%% are distinct.
It is guaranteed that the sum n⋅m%%ZSMJ29%% over all test cases does not exceed 106%%ZSMJ30%%.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the number of ways to restore the original complete path modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ31%%.

In the second test case, there is no suitable path, as the cells (1,1)%%ZSMJ34%% and (1,4)%%ZSMJ35%% do not have a common neighboring cell.
